Hi Alex —

Thanks for the clear list. We can absolutely provide everything you requested. Quick summary and attachments included below; Nikhil (cc'd) has added technical details and inline clarifications.

SSO
- We support SAML 2.0 (IdP-initiated and SP-initiated) and OpenID Connect.
- Attribute mapping: we surface standard attributes (email, name, groups) and allow custom attribute mapping rules per-tenant. You can require MFA enforcement by setting an IdP policy; we also support an SSO enforcement toggle at the org-level.

SCIM provisioning
- Full SCIM 2.0 compliance with PATCH, bulk, and GET support.
- Delta syncs via incremental endpoints and ETag handling; supports paged results for large directories.
- Group-to-role mapping: we provide a roleBindings mechanism where SCIM groups map to Redwood roles (see attached admin-role-matrix.csv). Nested groups are flattened by default but there is an opt-in recursive membership sync for customers that require it.

RBAC & Admin controls
- Role matrix attached (admin-role-matrix.csv). Out-of-the-box roles: Org Admin, Billing Admin, App Admin, Viewer, Support Read-Only.
- Delegation: Org Admins can create custom roles and delegate scopes to other users; we expose role templates via API and Console.
- Audit logging: all admin actions (role grants, config changes, SSO config edits) are recorded with actor, timestamp, IP, and request id. Default retention 90 days; enterprise retention up to 365 days available via contract.

Attachments (included)
- redwood_scim_samples.json (SCIM PATCH & POST examples)
- admin-role-matrix.csv (CSV mapping groups -> roles + scopes)
- sso_saml_flow_diagram.png (simple diagram for RFP appendix)

Next steps
- We can deliver the above attachments now (attached) and schedule a 30-minute technical call next week to walk through the SCIM schema and mapping examples. I'm available Wed/Thu 10:00–13:00 PT; please share a slot that works.

Regards,

Subject: Re: RFP clarification - provisioning, SSO, and admin controls (technical notes)

Alex — quick technical notes to supplement Marissa's summary:

SCIM specifics- We implement SCIM 2.0 core and enterprise extensions. Important implementation details:
  - PATCH: supported with both JSON Patch and SCIM patch operations.
  - Delta syncs: we support incremental sync via if-None-Match/ETag headers and provide a /Users?startIndex=...&count=... pattern for paging. For very large directories we recommend using incremental sync + lastModified filters.
  - Groups: nested groups are supported via a nestedMembers attribute; by default we flatten to direct membership for role assignment, but customers can enable recursive resolution for complex orgs.

Role mapping and API- RoleBindings: an internal mapping object maps SCIM group ID -> Redwood role ID. This mapping is editable via API and Console. RoleBindings support wildcards for prefix-based mappings (useful for department-based roles).

SAML / OIDC specifics- SAML: metadata import, certificate rotation schedule (we support auto-rotate via JWK endpoint), and attribute maps. We return role claims either as group attributes or as a custom Role claim depending on your IdP.
  - Recommended SAML attribute for roles: groups (type: urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:Group) or a custom attribute mapped to 'x-redwood-role'.
- OIDC: supports standard claims and token introspection endpoints; clients can scope down tokens for short-lived admin sessions.

Audit and retention- Admin actions are logged to our event store; logs include request payload hashes to support tamper detection. Exports: sysadmins can export audit records via Console or API as NDJSON. Retention default 90 days; archived retention (365+ days) on Enterprise contract.

Rate limits & performance- SCIM endpoints are rate-limited per-tenant; typical provisioning throughput is ~200 ops/sec per pool for dedicated customers. For high-volume provisioning we recommend batching combined with the bulk endpoint.

Attached: redwood_scim_samples.json (includes PATCH and group-resolution examples)

If you'd like, I can include a sample mapping snippet showing a nested group -> roleBinding example before your internal review.

-Nikhil
Principal Engineer, Identity Integrations
